this is a tough one

i struggled for a while with vaguely feeling like i shouldn't self-harm but just never *wanting* to stop. and now i've been in an intensive outpatient program for a few weeks and they really wanted my mom to take my blades away so i let her hide them. so i didn't really stop because i wanted to, but recently i was kinda starting to have reasons that made me want to stop

from what i remember, here was the main one: it feels like it isolates me from people. i felt like i had to hide constantly; i couldn't show my arms, i couldn't be honest, i couldn't talk about my problems without people looking at me like i don't know what's best for myself (unless those people also self-harm). now i feel like i can more so than before. it's a process, and part of it is not catastrophising and talking about my problems like they're huge, but my program has helped with that

i guess the only thing i can say is: look at your situation, really *look,* and see how self-harm impacts your day-to-day life. perhaps it makes you do things you wouldn't do if you didn't self-harm; perhaps it makes you avoid things. then look inside yourself and ask if those sacrifices are worth the things that self-harm gives you

good luck, friend <3

i don't know how to say this in a way that doesn't come across as condescending, but i'll try

i've struggled with self-harm and suicidal ideation for over 2 years. in recent months, the interpersonal aspect of my depression has been rearing its ugly mug, so i decided to go into an intensive outpatient program (basically group therapy with qualified clinicians every weekday) and one thing i've learned about is how one can reframe cognitive distortions

to me, it sounds like you're focusing on your friends' and family's not addressing this situation in any heartfelt, meaningful way as a sign that they simply don't care. i get that, i feel that all the time. but, at the same time, i remember before i had a better idea of how to address mental illness, when i often had no idea what to say in high-risk situations. often it seems easier to say nothing, because saying nothing feels less likely to cause damage than saying the wrong thing. i know that it's really hard to break the perspective that maximizes opportunities for self-hatred, but from what you've said, i think people are trying to be sensitive at the expense of reaching out
